info.title: ipterm
info.summary: IP address, network (ASN), DNS, email security (SPF, DMARC, DKIM), domain report card, registry (whois) and subnet lookups for curl and scripts.
info.description:
No key and no sign-up. Command-line clients (curl, wget, HTTPie, PowerShell...) and scripts get JSON; browsers get an HTML page at the same address, so send `?format=json` from a browser-like client to be sure of JSON. Add `?format=text` to any lookup for aligned key/value lines instead of JSON (quote the URL in a shell), or `/text` after an address or AS number (`/8.8.8.8/text`, `/AS13335/text`: nothing to quote; `/json` for JSON). `?color=1` adds ANSI colors to a text answer; they are never on by default. One-value endpoints answer with a single line of plain text; a missing value is an empty line with HTTP 404. Uncached lookups are limited to 30 a minute per address (IPv6: per /64), after which the answer is HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header; your own `/json` and `/text` still answer past it, without the hostname. No cookies or tracking, and ipterm's code stores and logs nothing about callers; Cloudflare, which hosts it, keeps its own request analytics and security events (https://ipterm.net/privacy). Plain-text reference: `curl ipterm.net/help`.

IP address data powered by IPinfo (https://ipinfo.io), used under CC BY-SA 4.0. Networks: RIPEstat. Registry records: RDAP from the regional internet registries and domain registries. DNS and mail checks: Cloudflare's public resolver (1.1.1.1), plus each domain's own MTA-STS policy file.

get.description: The only one-value endpoint for your own address that asks anybody: Cloudflare's resolver. Counts toward the rate limit.

get.summary: A terminal card for your own address, with a Braille world map
get.description: Your IP, network (AS number and name), city, region and country, time zone (with the local time) and the Cloudflare data center that answered, under a small world map with your approximate location lit. From Cloudflare's edge only: no outside call, no reverse DNS, and it doesn't count toward the rate limit. ANSI colors by default for command-line clients (curl, wget, HTTPie, PowerShell). Browsers are redirected to the terminal page (/).

parameters.name: w
parameters.description: Width in columns, frame included; values outside 32 to 120 are brought within them. `curl "ipterm.net/me?w=$COLUMNS"` fits the terminal.

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: 0 for no ANSI colors, 1 to force them. Default: on for command-line clients, off for other HTTP clients.

parameters.name: redact
parameters.description: Present (`?redact`): the IP address is replaced with x's, for screenshots. The rest of the card is unchanged.

200.description: The card: about 20 lines of UTF-8 text (box drawing and Braille characters).

get.summary: Your IP, network, country and data center on one line
get.description: For shell prompts and tmux status bars. From Cloudflare's edge only: no outside call, no rate limit. Parts that aren't known are left out.

get.summary: 200 if your address is on the given network or in the given country, 412 if not
get.description: For scripts that must stop when a VPN drops: `curl -fs ipterm.net/expect/AS13335 || <stop something>`. Compared with Cloudflare's own data for the request (as /asn and /cc), so there is no outside call and no rate limit.

parameters.name: values
parameters.description: An AS number (AS13335, or just 13335) or a two-letter country code (ISO 3166-1; Cloudflare uses T1 for Tor), or up to 10 of them separated by commas: any one matching is enough. Case doesn't matter.

200.description: A match: the value that matched, in canonical form.

400.description: Not an AS number or country code, or more than 10.

412.description: No match. The line says what the request came from.

text/plain.example: no match: expected AS13335, but this request came from AS7922 in US

get.summary: A, AAAA, MX, NS, TXT and CAA records, the host of the first address, and DNSSEC
get.description: With an IP address as the name: its reverse DNS (PTR). A nonexistent domain answers 200 with status NXDOMAIN.

get.summary: One record type, with TTLs
Email security check: MX, SPF, DMARC, DKIM, MTA-STS, TLS-RPT and BIMI, graded A to F
get.description: Every finding is a line with a status (ok, warn, fail or info) and, for warn and fail, a fix. The grade counts them: A no FAIL and no WARN; B no FAIL, one or two WARN; C one FAIL, or three or more WARN; D two FAIL; F three or more FAIL, no working SPF and no DMARC, or SPF that lets any server pass (+all). INFO never counts. SPF includes and redirects are followed to count DNS lookups against RFC 7208's limit of 10. DKIM selectors can't be listed, so the common ones are tried (google, selector1, selector2, default, k1, s1), plus the one named in ?dkim=; finding none is info. The MTA-STS policy is fetched from https://mta-sts.{domain}/.well-known/mta-sts.txt (redirects are not followed). A nonexistent domain answers 200 with status NXDOMAIN and grade null. Cached for five minutes.

get.summary: Domain report card: DNSSEC, IPv6, CAA and HTTPS records, the email security grade, expiry and transfer lock, and the website's HTTPS redirect and security headers, graded A to F
get.description: Every finding is a line with a status (ok, warn, fail or info) and, for warn and fail, a fix. The grade counts them: A no FAIL and no WARN; B no FAIL, one to three WARN; C one FAIL, or four or more WARN; D two FAIL; F three or more FAIL, an expired registration, or broken DNSSEC (validating resolvers refuse the domain). INFO never counts, and neither does a part that couldn't be checked (listed in notChecked). DNS comes from Cloudflare's resolver (DNSSEC, AAAA, CAA at the name or its closest parent, HTTPS). The mail line is the mail check's grade (A ok, B warn, C or worse fail) with its main findings in details. The registration (RDAP) gives expiry (warn within 30 days, fail once expired or lapsing) and the transfer lock. The website gets one HEAD request to https://{domain}/ (a GET, its body dropped unread, if the site refuses HEAD; redirects followed only within the domain, at most twice, never to plain http) for HSTS, Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, frame protection and Referrer-Policy, and one to http://{domain}/ for the redirect to HTTPS; a 403, a bot challenge, a timeout or an error is info (couldn't check), never fail. Certificates aren't checked. A nonexistent domain answers 200 with status NXDOMAIN and grade null. Cached for five minutes (one minute when a part couldn't be checked and a recheck might fill it). Never uses IPinfo or proxycheck.io.

get.summary: The report card's grade as a shields.io endpoint badge
get.description: For README badges: ![domain security grade](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https%3A%2F%2Fipterm.net%2Fbadge%2Fexample.com.json). shields.io (and GitHub's image proxy) fetch this, so readers' browsers never contact ipterm. The message is the grade letter, colored brightgreen (A) to red (F); "no such domain", "checking…" (the card wasn't ready within about three seconds; it finishes in the background) or "busy, try later" otherwise. Cached for an hour (ten minutes when part of the card couldn't be checked and a recheck might fill it), and a cached copy is sent with the time it has left; a card that can't be had falls back to the last grade, kept for a week.

400.description: Not a domain name: the same badge shape, with isError.

get.summary: The same badge drawn by ipterm, as SVG
get.description: Each reader's browser fetches this from ipterm directly (unless a proxy such as GitHub's sits in between), so prefer the shields.io endpoint where readers' privacy matters. Sent with Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: cross-origin so other sites can show it. Cached like the JSON.

400.description: Not a domain name (a grey badge).

get.summary: Registry record (RDAP) for an IP address, AS number or domain
get.description: Addresses and networks: owner, address block, dates and abuse contact. Domains: registrar, registration and expiry dates, status, name servers, DNSSEC and abuse contact; owner details are usually redacted.

404.description: No record (found: false, often with a message explaining why).

get.summary: Subnet calculator (IPv4 and IPv6); pure calculation, no outside calls (for how a public range is routed, see /route/{network}/{prefix})
How a public prefix is routed (BGP): the route that carries it, the origin network, RPKI, RIS visibility and sample AS paths, from RIPEstat. Browsers are sent to the prefix's /cidr page

200.description: The routing. Cached for six hours.

get.summary: The route a public address is in, as for /route/{network}/{prefix}
Is TCP port n open on your own IP? (command-line clients; browsers get a page explaining the port)
get.description: The server opens one TCP connection to the address the request comes from (never any other) on port n, sends nothing and closes it, and reports open (accepted), closed (turned away at once: nothing listening, or a firewall rejected it), no-answer (nothing within 5 seconds: filtered, or not forwarded) or untestable (port 25, which Cloudflare blocks; Cloudflare's own addresses, such as WARP; non-public addresses, including reserved and IPv4-embedding IPv6 forms such as 6to4 and Teredo). Runs only for command-line user agents (curl, wget, HTTPie, PowerShell) or same-origin requests from the ipterm page; other callers get HTTP 403. Search crawlers and link previews get the page explaining the port. Limited to 10 checks a minute per address. Use `curl -4` to test your IPv4 address, where router port forwards apply: over IPv6 the IPv6 address is tested. Only TCP can be tested.

403.description: Not a command-line client or a same-origin request.

429.description: More than 10 port checks in a minute from your address.

get.summary: A leak test result someone shared: the grade, whether a VPN was on, and which checks passed, leaked or weren't tested
get.description: The link `share` gives after the leak test (`leaktest` in the browser terminal, or https://ipterm.net/leaktest). Its code is made in that browser (public/leakgrade.js): version 1, the grade letter, then two Crockford base32 characters holding whether a VPN was detected and each graded check's flag. It holds nothing else, no IP address, provider, location or DNS resolver, so the answer is decoded from the code alone: nothing is looked up, tested or stored, and it doesn't count toward the rate limit. A code whose grade doesn't match its checks is not valid. Command-line clients get JSON (`?format=text` for aligned lines); browsers get a noindex page with a "run yours" link, which never runs the test by itself. Cached for a day.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: The result code, in either case. 1bjp is a B on a VPN, with only the time zone leaking.

text/plain.example:
grade        B
vpn          a VPN was on
DNS          no leak
WebRTC       no leak
IPv6 / IPv4  no leak
time zone    leaked

404.description: Not a leak test result code. Browsers get a 404 page.

get.summary: Which DNS resolvers looked up your test names (the DNS leak test)
get.description: Look up one or more random names <token>.dl.ipterm.net first (tokens: 20 lowercase hex characters; each answers NXDOMAIN), then ask here within two minutes. Lists the resolvers that asked for them, with their networks (IPinfo Lite); each token's answer is given once. Command-line clients and the ipterm page only. Example: T=$(openssl rand -hex 10); dig +short $T.dl.ipterm.net; curl "ipterm.net/api/dnsleak?t=$T"

seen.description: How many of the tokens were looked up

service.description: A public DNS service, when the network is one: Cloudflare (1.1.1.1), Google Public DNS (8.8.8.8), Quad9 (9.9.9.9), Cisco OpenDNS

403.description: Not a command-line client or a same-origin request.

404.description: The DNS leak test isn't set up on this server.

get.summary: Address-bar search: a redirect to the page for an address, network, domain, range, email address or port
get.description: For browsers (the target of /opensearch.xml and of the search form on /api). q is anything the terminal takes: an IP address, an AS number, a domain or URL, a range or an address and netmask, an email address (its mail check), port <n>, or a command such as `dig gmail.com MX` or `whois AS13335`. The answer is a 302 to that page on this site; follow it with curl -L. An empty q goes to /. Input it can't read is a 400.

302.description: To the matching page, always a path on this site.

400.description: Nothing it could look up. JSON with `error` and `suggest` (for a bare number: its ASN and port pages); browsers get a page.

get.summary: The command-line reference as plain text
get.description: Browsers are redirected to the /api page.

get.summary: API docs: an HTML page for browsers, the /help text for command-line clients

Attribution.description: The IPinfo credit, on /{ip}/{field} answers that come from IPinfo (every field except hostname; not on the answers about your own address, which come from Cloudflare). Sent as a header so the body stays one line for $(curl ...).
Attribution.example: IP address data powered by IPinfo (https://ipinfo.io)

Noindex.description: On the /text and /json path forms: search engines leave these copies of the /{ip} and /AS{number} pages out.

format.name: format
format.description: json: JSON even for browser-like clients. text: aligned key/value lines instead of JSON.

formatText.name: format
formatText.description: text: your details as aligned key/value lines instead of the bare address.

color.name: color
color.description: 1: ANSI colors in a text answer (format=text or a /text path), on the key column and the verdict that starts the vpn / proxy line, for reading in a terminal. 0 or absent: none, the default, so pipes into grep, awk or jq never see escape codes. JSON is never colored.

block.name: block
block.description: 0: no block in the answer, and no request to the address's registry for it. Your own address never gets one either way.

lite.name: lite
lite.description: 1: the network and country only (IPinfo Lite, as /{ip}/{field} uses), with no VPN / proxy check (no flags or privacy), so the lookup spends neither the IPinfo Core nor the proxycheck.io budget. The terminal's leak test looks up your other IP version this way: it compares only that address's network. Your own address is answered from the edge either way.

mailDomain.name: domain
mailDomain.description: Domain name (international names are converted to punycode)

gradeDomain.name: domain
gradeDomain.description: Domain name (international names are converted to punycode); a subdomain is graded as itself, with its registered domain's registration. A DNS record name, with a label starting with _ (_dmarc.gmail.com), is not a domain: 400

dkim.name: dkim
dkim.description: A DKIM selector to check as well as the common ones: the s= value in a message's DKIM-Signature header

dnsName.name: name
dnsName.description: Domain name (international names are converted to punycode) or an IP address for reverse DNS

OneValue.description: One line: the value and a newline.

NoValue.description: No value is known: an empty line.

BadRequest.description: Not a valid or not a public input.

RateLimited.description: More than 30 uncached lookups in a minute from your address.

Upstream.description: A data source didn't respond. Try again in a moment.

RouteBot.description: An automated visitor (crawler, link preview, AI agent) asking for routing nobody has looked up in the last six hours: RIPEstat isn't asked for bots. The prefixes 1.1.1.0/24, 8.8.8.0/24 and 9.9.9.0/24 always answer when asked by prefix (/route/8.8.8.0/24), not by an address in them.

grade.description: A: no leaks; B: only the time zone leaks; C: DNS leaks, but neither WebRTC nor IPv6; D: WebRTC or IPv6 leaks (one of the two), and DNS doesn't; F: WebRTC or IPv6 and DNS, or WebRTC and IPv6. Only leaks past a VPN count

enum: couldn't tell whether a VPN was on

checks.description: Each graded check: DNS, WebRTC, the other IP version (IPv6 or IPv4) and the time zone

ip.description: The address that was tested: the one the request came from

ms.description: How long the connection took to be accepted or turned away (5000 for no-answer)

notes.description: What the result means and what to check: IPv6, UDP, port forwarding, carrier-grade NAT

service.description: What the port is commonly used for, when it is one of the ports ipterm describes

colo.description: Your own address only: the Cloudflare data center

flags.description: IPinfo Core (without a token, IPinfo's free API gives anycast only)

privacy.description: proxycheck.io's VPN / proxy / Tor opinion, when configured (never with lite=1)

vpnServer.description: Present only when a VPN provider's own published server list names the address (Mullvad, Private Internet Access, IVPN and AirVPN, downloaded every 6 hours; NordVPN's terms forbid automated access, Proton VPN's list has no public route and Surfshark's encrypts the addresses). Exact addresses only, searched in ipterm's own copy, so it costs nothing and every caller gets it, crawlers and AI assistants too (not with lite=1). None of these lists names the addresses traffic leaves from, so today every listed address is an entry. An address on no list proves nothing either way. The vpn / proxy line of the text answer and the page words it.

role.description: entry: the provider's users connect to this address, and sites may see them at a different one. exit: the provider says its users reach sites from it

listUpdated.description: When ipterm last downloaded that provider's list (a list not refreshed for 3 days is no longer used)

block.description: When the registry record of the most specific network the address is in was created (RDAP, the record whois shows). Lookups of a public address only (/{ip}, /{ip}/json, /api/lookup?ip=; /{ip}/text gets the line below instead), not /json, the one-value routes, block=0 or the caller's own address (it is never sent to a registry, asked for by number or not). Left out when the registry has no date, hadn't answered within about 0.3 seconds of the rest of the answer (its record is then cached for the next lookup: try again a moment later), failed in the last minute (ten after a 429), or the caller is past the rate limit; crawlers and link previews get it only once someone else's lookup or whois has cached the record. recent: within the last 180 days. Location databases often take months to catch up with new or reassigned blocks, so for a recent block sites may disagree about where the address is; the text answer adds a block line saying so.

network.description: The network's CIDR blocks (comma-separated), or its first and last address

registry.description: The registry that holds the record: ARIN, RIPE NCC, APNIC, LACNIC or AFRINIC, or the national registry that keeps it for one of them, such as IDNIC, JPNIC, KRNIC, TWNIC or NIC.br (whois's registry). A name, not a server's hostname; null when not known

registered.description: The date part of the registry's own timestamp

days.description: Calendar days from registered to today (UTC)

upstreams.description: The networks RIPEstat sees just before this one in AS paths, by how many RIS peers see each (usually its transit providers). null if RIPEstat didn't answer; tooMany for large transit networks, whose neighbour list isn't read

query.description: The prefix (as its network) or address asked about

status.description: announced: the prefix itself is a route; covered: it (or the address) is inside a less specific route; split: not announced as a whole, but as more specific prefixes; unrouted: no RIS peer sees a route that covers it

visibility.description: RIS peers that see the route, of those that send a full table

upstreams.description: The networks just before the origin in the sampled routes, most common first

paths.description: Sample AS paths, prepending collapsed, the origin last

inside.description: Up to 8 more specific routes inside the prefix

value.description: The record's data. For MX, the mail server, or "." for a null MX (RFC 7505: the domain accepts no mail).

status.description: The resolver's answer to the domain's MX query; only NOERROR is graded

providers.description: Recognized from the MX host names, e.g. Google Workspace, Microsoft 365

redirectMacro.description: true: the record hands off to a redirect= with a macro (%{...}), which isn't followed, so all is null without meaning there is none

counted.description: false: counting stopped once past the limit

unanswered.description: Selectors the resolver couldn't read (SERVFAIL after a retry, or no answer): not checked, and not reported as having no key

unread.description: Records the resolver couldn't read, with its answer (e.g. SPF: SERVFAIL, or DMARC: no answer): reported, not graded as missing. A subdomain without a DMARC record of its own has DMARC unread when a parent's _dmarc couldn't be read

subrequests.description: DNS queries and fetches the check took

status.description: The resolver's answer for the domain. SERVFAIL with a grade is broken DNSSEC (grade F); otherwise only NOERROR is graded

details.description: On the mail line: the mail check's main findings

skipped.description: On info lines for a part that couldn't be checked: what the grade leaves out

lasting.description: On a skipped line whose gap a recheck won't fill (the TLD has no RDAP or the registry has no record of the name, a non-public address, a 401, 403 or bot challenge, a site that serves only HTTPS, no CAA in the parent names asked). Only true; absent otherwise

notChecked.description: Parts that couldn't be checked, e.g. "security headers" after a 403 or a timeout

broken.description: The Extended DNS Error when validation fails

from.description: The name the records were found at (the domain or its closest parent)

web.description: skipped: noaddr, private or unread (an A or AAAA answer couldn't be read) when the site wasn't asked

headers.description: The security headers read from the final page (lowercase names, values capped at 1,000 characters)

markdown.description: A README badge drawn by shields.io

markdownSvg.description: The same badge served by ipterm

subrequests.description: DNS queries, the mail check's fetches and requests to the site for this card (not counting whois or cache reads)

Badge.description: shields.io's endpoint schema, and nothing else (it refuses unknown keys).

registry.description: An address's or ASN's: the registry that holds the record, as in IpInfo's block.registry. A domain's: the registry that runs its extension (Verisign for .com), or its RDAP server's hostname when ipterm doesn't know its name
